data.narrative: Completed Module 6 Parallel Agent Management - chose interface-first parallelization with manual merge strategy. Created interface contracts for 3 agents: Comment Threads, @Mention Parsing, Audit Log. Fixed integration gap with glue code bridging event bus to audit log. Verified individual features, cross-feature integration, conflict detection. Updated contracts with system-level integration contract. Learned interface-first prevents conflicts, system-level contracts necessary, sequential integration safer.

dimension_scores.observation: Interface contracts specific: defines creates, reads, modifies, data shapes, API endpoints, integration points, events. Each agent gets locked specification. Agents run parallel against fixed interfaces. Prevents catastrophic conflicts without over-constraining.
dimension_scores.evidence: interface-contracts.md: 'Agent 1 Comment Threads: creates Comment model, endpoints, emits events. Agent 2 @Mention: creates parser utility, notification service, standalone. Agent 3 Audit Log: creates AuditLog model, middleware, consumes events. Contracts define exact data shapes and integration points.'

dimension_scores.observation: Three-level verification: Level 1 Individual features work (comments CRUD, @mention parsing, audit log), Level 2 Cross-feature integration (comment with @mention triggers parser/notification, comment audit-logged), Level 3 Conflict detection (no files modified by multiple agents, migrations clean, test suite passes). Identified integration gap - comment events not reaching audit log.
dimension_scores.evidence: interface-contracts.md: 'System-level integration contract added: Event bus format, audit log integration options, resource type registry. Glue code subscribes to comment.* events, calls auditLog.record().'

dimension_scores.observation: Fixed integration gap with targeted glue prompt instead of re-running entire agent. Wrote small integration module bridging event bus to audit log. Sequential integration: merged Agent 1 first, tested, then Agent 2, then Agent 3. Each merge built on stable foundation. Avoided expensive re-runs. 4 parallel agents completed in roughly 1 hour vs 3 hours sequential.
dimension_scores.evidence: Fix: 'Glue prompt: subscribe to comment.* events, call auditLog.record(), map to audit log entries. Keep minimal - glue code not new feature.'

dimension_scores.observation: Chose interface-first over branch-and-merge. Prevents conflicts by defining interfaces upfront. Branch-and-merge risk: 4 agents modifying same model differently causes conflicts, merge cost exceeds parallelism savings. Chose manual merge over agent-assisted for full control. AI merging AI output compounds errors. Sequential integration safer though partially defeats parallelism purpose - safety worth cost.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision: 'Interface-first: define all interfaces up front before agents run. Each agent gets locked specification. Outputs merge cleanly because connection points defined before building. Manual merge: review all outputs, identify conflicts, manually integrate. Full control despite time cost.'

dimension_scores.observation: Shipped 3 parallel features (comments, @mentions, audit log) with cross-feature integration verified. Individual features work, integration works, no conflicts detected. Full test suite passes. System-level integration contract added to prevent future integration gaps. Glue code bridges event bus to audit log. Quality: structural 4, surface 4.
dimension_scores.evidence: interface-contracts.md: 'System-level integration contract: Event bus format {resourceType.action}, audit integration options, resource type registry. Verified: comment create/update/delete appear in audit log with correct resourceType.'

strengths: System-level integration contract added to prevent future gaps
Glue code efficiently bridged event bus to audit log
Sequential integration with testing at each merge step
data.recommendation: Module 6 complete. Ready for remaining modules.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Reflection: 'Interface-first strategy defines connection points before agents run. Each agent gets locked specification. Outputs merge cleanly because connection points defined before building. Prevents catastrophic conflicts without over-constraining.'

Reflection: 'Individual agent contracts necessary but not sufficient. Need system-level contracts describing how system parts connect: event bus format, audit integration options, resource type registry.'

Reflection: 'Parallel execution speed (3x) but introduces merge problem. Interface contracts prevent conflicts by defining how agents interact. Sequential integration with testing at each merge step safer than parallel merge.'
